name: Global food prices
summary: FAO food price index eased to 133.9 in October, below the 135 Alert line but up 5.9% on a year
state: The FAO Food Price Index fell 1.2% to 133.9 in October, as reported on 6 Nov, with cereals down 4.5% and sugar up 6.6% (IndexBox, citing FAO). That is below the 135 Alert line but 5.9% higher than a year earlier, meeting the Watch line; September's 136.0 was the highest since 2022 (FAO). The status steps down from Alert to Watch.
for_you: Food import bills remain high for import-dependent countries, and supermarket prices tend to follow world prices with a lag of months.
rubric_hit: FFPI 133.9 in the 120–135 Watch band; y/y +5.9% > +5%

sources.title: IndexBox — FAO Food Price Index drops 1.2% in October 2026

why: Food prices drive inflation, hunger and political unrest; poorer countries spend up to half of income on food.
drivers: Harvests, weather, fertiliser and energy costs, export bans, conflict in breadbaskets.

rubric.alert: FFPI > 135, or multiple major exporters ban exports of a staple.
rubric.watch: FFPI 120–135, or y/y > +5%, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: FAO Food Price Index < 120 and y/y change < +5%.
